paragraphs.text: Verify and export the references your DeepSeek Harness conversation already cited.
# dsh-refkeeper
**English** · 简体中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-refkeeper) [](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)
A DeepSeek Harness plugin. It reads a conversation, collects the papers that conversation cited, che
cks each paper against Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv and DataCite, and exports the confirmed entries as
BibTeX or RIS. Papers that fail the check go into a separate quarantine file instead of the library.
If this plugin saves you time, a star on GitHub helps other people find it. If you hit a bug or want
a feature, open an issue — Chinese or English, either is fine. I read all of them and add the usefu
l ones to the roadmap.
## What it does
- **Collects citations.** Scope can be one turn, the last N turns, or the whole session. It recognis
es DOIs, arXiv ids, ISBNs and report numbers, and also reference lines written in APA, GB/T 7714 or

IEEE style.
- **Checks them against registries.** An entry is accepted only if the title matches, th

e year is within one year, the first author matches, and at least one registry returned a record.
-
**Writes annotations.** After a capture, the model already running the session writes four short fie
lds per entry: a summary, why the paper is relevant here, a supporting quote, and caveats. A quote t

hat does not appear in the conversation is dropped.
- **Exports.** BibTeX, RIS, or both. The export
can cover the last capture, the entries you ticked, or the whole library.
## One button in the composer
The interface gains exactly one thing: an item in the composer's tool row, standing next to the work
-mode and model pickers. It reads `❝ Refs` (Chinese UI: `❝ 引用`). There is no sidebar, no toolbar and
no floating widget — press it and the capture panel opens in the top-right corner of the window, cl
ose it and the row is back to what it was.
## Why not just copy the citations by hand
For three papers, copy by hand. Past that it is slow and easy to get wrong: one DOI sits in a tool r
esult, an APA line sits in a summary, another paper is only mentioned by name two turns earlier.
Asking the model for a `.bib` file is faster, but models make up page ranges, DOIs and author order,
and the mistake is usually found at submission time.
| | Copy by hand | Ask a model for a `.bib` | This plugin |
| Source of the list | your reading | the model's memory | parsed from the conversation you select |

| Metadata checked | no | no | Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv, DataCite |
| What happens to a paper that

cannot be confirmed | n/a | kept | moved to `refs/quarantine.json`, excluded from export |
| Invent
ed pages, DOIs, authors | n/a | possible | fields come from registry records; unsupported fields sta

y empty |
| Why the paper is there | lost | lost | annotation plus a verbatim quote |
| Same export

twice | n/a | unlikely | identical bytes; entries sorted, citekeys stable |
| Citations you never us
ed | not included | included | excluded by default: tool output is not treated as a citation |
## Install
In DSH open **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `dsh-refkeeper`. The package is published
on npm, so this is one step and runs no build: the tarball ships the built `lib/`. Enable it for the
current profile, then reload.
To track the repository instead of the published version, paste the Git address `https://github.com/
ymwang92/dsh-refkeeper` into the same dialog. The repository commits `lib/` too, so that route needs
eeper` into the same dialog. The repository commits `lib/` too, so that route needs no build either.
## Use

1. Open a conversation that cited papers and open the capture panel above the composer.
2. Choose th

e scope, then **Capture & save**.
3. The panel lists what was saved and what went to the ⚠ quarantin

e. Untick any entry you do not want.
4. Choose BibTeX and/or RIS, then **Export this capture**.
The same steps as commands:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Files are written to `refs/` inside the session's workspace. To export into a specific folder, paste
its path in the panel once; it is remembered in `refs/settings.json`. Folders outside the session w
orkspace are refused, because the host only allows writes inside it.
## What the output looks like
`refs/annotated.md` is the reading copy:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
and the matching BibTeX entry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
If the citation in the conversation lacked volume, issue, pages, publisher or language, those come f
rom the registry record. Fields that neither the conversation nor a registry supports are left out o
f the file entirely.
## How a paper is accepted or rejected
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`unverified` is a third status, used when the registries could not be reached. The entry stays in th
e library and can be retried later; a network failure is not evidence that a citation is wrong. `qua
rantined` means the registries answered and disagreed.
## Annotations
Four fields: `summary`, `relevance`, `evidence`, `caveats`. They are written after a capture by the
profile's default model, from the conversation lines that mention the paper. A prompt rule and a par
ser filter both reject sentences that describe the absence of information ("the excerpt does not men
tion this work"); such a field is stored as empty and omitted from the export, so BibTeX gets no emp
ty `note` and RIS gets no empty `N1`.
The model call happens once per capture, with a 60 second cap, and covers at most 12 entries. Entrie
s beyond that budget, or captures without a reachable model, keep their bibliographic fields and the
capture result says why annotations were skipped. The `ref_save` tool still accepts annotations you
write yourself, and existing user annotations are never overwritten.
## Chinese references
GB/T 7714 reference lines are parsed along with APA and IEEE. Chinese titles are matched against reg
istry records by character bigrams (Dice ≥ 0.90) rather than word tokens, because romanised records
otherwise never match. `language` is carried into both export formats.
[该节后续省略]
## Data and privacy
- Requests leave the machine only for verification: the identifier or title is sent to Crossref, Ope

nAlex, arXiv and DataCite.
- Annotations use the model already configured in the session; the plugin

holds no API key of its own.
- No telemetry. The library is a local file.
